title: Interim or full service: which one do you need?
summary: The right service depends on your mileage and how long it has been since the last one. Here is a simple way to decide.
image_alt: Illustration of a car on a workshop lift
author: The Kestrel Garage team

body.p: An interim service covers the essentials, such as oil, filter and safety checks. A full service adds more checks and replacement parts.
Your handbook sets the intervals for your car. If you drive a lot of miles, an interim service between full services can help.

body.callout: Bring your service history when you visit so we can see what was done last time.
